From: Emma Roberts <emma.roberts@arcadiagen.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Scoped tenant log preservation for ArcadiaGen regulator audit

Hi Chloe,

We have an upcoming regulatory audit for a specific product line and the regulator has asked us to retain tenant-level telemetry and debug traces for a particular production tenant (AG-Prod-06) for 180 days instead of your standard 60-day ephemeral policy. The ask is scoped to this single tenant and is limited to debug/session traces and system telemetry (no full request payloads or PII).

Can Redwood accept a timeboxed, tenant-scoped exception? If yes, we need:
- A short description of the retention boundary (what artifacts will be retained)
- Evidence artifacts we can include in our audit pack (retention matrix, proof-of-delete workflow, CAIQ/SIG/SOC2 artifacts)
- A recommended mutual action plan (we can sign an agreement to limit scope & duration)

We need to respond to the regulator within two weeks. Looping in ArcadiaGen legal (legal@arcadiagen.com).

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Roberts
Head of IT Compliance, ArcadiaGen
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Roberts <emma.roberts@arcadiagen.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: Scoped tenant log preservation for ArcadiaGen regulator audit

Emma — thanks for the details, and sorry you're under a tight timeline. We can potentially support a scoped tenant-specific retention exception if the scope and controls are well-defined. Quick clarifying questions before we scope a proposal: 

1) Confirm exactly which artifact categories you need preserved (e.g., debug traces, session indices, request/response headers, token-level logs). You already indicated no PII/request payloads — thanks.
2) Do you have a preferred start/end date for the 180-day window, or should we treat this as retroactive for AG-Prod-06 (if so, when does the window begin)?
3) Is ArcadiaGen willing to sign a timeboxed Addendum that limits the exception to AG-Prod-06 and requires Redwood to delete retained artifacts after the agreed window?

I'll loop in Security/Product to confirm operational feasibility and produce the artifacts you requested (retention matrix + evidence pack). Attaching a template SAR/MAP we typically use for these exceptions; if you can sign the MAP, we can expedite.

On internal notes, cc'ing Irene and Ben to validate feasibility and to estimate work effort.

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Chloe — forwarding my quick feasibility notes after an ops sync with Priyom: 

On Tue, 6 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700, Chloe Martin wrote:
> Emma — thanks for the details, and sorry you're under a tight timeline. We can potentially support a scoped tenant-specific retention exception if the scope and controls are well-defined...

Operational summary:
- We can retain "debug traces" and session indices for a single tenant by turning on a tenant-specific retention flag for AG-Prod-06 that overrides the default ephemeral TTL. That will route those traces to a segregated retention bucket for 180 days.
- We must be explicit about what we will not retain: full request/response bodies, uploaded files, and any PII-derived fields. Those must be redacted or excluded by our ingestion filter.
- Engineering (Priyom) estimates ~2–3 days of low-priority work to enable the tenant override, add a retention label, and produce an automated deletion job and audit log entry on deletion. We'll need an approval window to schedule the change (can be done in staging and then prod).
- There's a small compliance risk if the retained artifacts can be correlated back to user identities; we'll require ArcadiaGen to provide an operational justification and sign the MAP that restricts use cases (forensics only).

Next steps recommended:
1) Get signed MAP from ArcadiaGen limiting scope & duration.
2) We provide: retention matrix CSV, deletion attestations template, CAIQ/SIG extracts mapping retained artifacts to control identifiers, short runbook for review.
3) Priyom will create the tenant override and deletion job once MAP is signed.

Irene — please confirm the audit artifacts we should provide for the regulator (SOC2 extract, SIG mapping). Chloe — happy to draft the packet once we confirm.

—Ben
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Roberts <emma.roberts@arcadiagen.com>, Legal <legal@arcadiagen.com>

Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Scoped tenant log preservation for ArcadiaGen regulator audit

Emma / ArcadiaGen Legal — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on internal review, Redwood can support a timeboxed, tenant-scoped retention exception for AG-Prod-06 under these conditions: 

Scope (what Redwood will retain)
- Debug traces (structured debug logs without raw request/response bodies)
- Session indices and system telemetry (service-level metrics and event traces)
- Audit logs of access to retained artifacts (access will be logged and recorded)

Exclusions (what will NOT be retained)
- Full request/response payloads, file uploads, and attachments
- Any fields identified as PII in ArcadiaGen's data classification

Controls and deliverables (what Redwood will provide)
- Retention matrix (CSV) mapping artifact types to retention periods and control mappings — attached: redwood_retention_matrix.csv
- Proof-of-delete runbook and deletion attestations template we will sign after the 180-day window
- CAIQ/SIG mapping extract that cites the controls we rely on (we will provide the extract in the evidence pack)
- Implementation timeline and change tickets (we'll schedule the tenant override work once the MAP is signed)

Operational notes and obligations from ArcadiaGen
- ArcadiaGen must sign the provided Mutual Action Plan (attached: arcadiagen_sar_template.pdf) limiting the exception to AG-Prod-06, forensics-only use, and agreeing to redaction responsibilities for any PII.
- ArcadiaGen must nominate a single technical contact (we have you listed as Emma) and a legal signatory.

Timeline
- If MAP is signed within 3 business days, engineering can enable the tenant retention override in staging within 2 business days and in prod within 3–5 business days thereafter.

Next steps
1) Please review the attached retention matrix and SAR/MAP.
2) If acceptable, return a signed MAP to chloe.martin@redwood.com and legal@redwood.com.
3) We'll schedule the change and provide the evidence pack for your audit folder: https://redwood.example.com/drive/arcadiagen-retention-pack

Attachments (stubs):
- arcadiagen_sar_template.pdf (MAP/short addendum)
- redwood_retention_matrix.csv (artifact -> TTL -> control mapping)

If you prefer a short call to walk through the artifacts, I can set up a 30-min slot tomorrow.

Best,
Chloe Martin
